message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most celebrated and influential composers who have made their mark in the United States:

| Composer | Era / Style | Notable Works |
|----------|-------------|---------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | Jazz‑Classical Fusion | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | Neoclassical/“American” Sound | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | Broadway & Classical | *West Side Story*, *Candide* |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks* |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film Scores | *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalism | *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910–1981) | Modernist | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **Charles Ives** (1874–1954) | Experimental | *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata* |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | Post‑Minimalism | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* |
| **William Grant Still** (1895–1978) | “Third Stream” (Jazz + Classical) | *Afro-American Symphony*, *Bluebird* |

These composers span a wide range of styles—from early jazz influences to contemporary minimalism—and each has contributed significantly to both American and global music culture.
